findings.text: ICMPv6 user API defines Time Exceeded subcodes with hop limit exceeded as zero and fragment reassembly time exceeded as one, and Parameter Problem subcodes with erroneous header field as zero, unrecognized next header as one, unrecognized option as two, and incomplete header as three.

ICMPv6 extended echo uses type one hundred sixty for request and one hundred sixty one for reply. Packet filtering uses socket option number one, with actions block as one, pass as two, block others as three, and pass only as four.
Filtering state is a structure holding eight unsigned thirty two bit words in an array called data, providing two hundred fifty six bits for type based pass or block decisions.

Multicast Listener Discovery version two defines record kinds one through six in order include mode, exclude mode, change to include, change to exclude, allow new sources, and block old sources. It also defines an initializer for the all multicast capable routers group as Internet Protocol version six address with leading bytes ff zero two and trailing byte hex sixteen, zeros elsewhere.

Network interface user API limits the interface name to sixteen bytes, the alias to two hundred fifty six bytes, the alternative name to one hundred twenty eight bytes, and the hardware address length used by interface requests to six bytes.

Device flags occupy single bits zero through eighteen in order up, broadcast, debug, loopback, point to point, no trailers, running, no address resolution, promiscuous, all multicast, master, slave, multicast, port select, auto media, dynamic, lower up, dormant, and echo. The first sixteen are exposed under one user API gate and the last three under a second gate. Short macros alias each enumerator to itself for source compatibility.

A volatile mask combines nine flags that kernel may change asynchronously, namely loopback, point to point, broadcast, echo, master, slave, running, lower up, and dormant. Two query selectors exist with value one for interface hardware description and value two for protocol description.

Serial interface hardware kinds use hex values one zero zero zero through one zero zero six in listed order for V thirty five, V twenty four, X twenty one, T one, E one, synchronous serial that software cannot set, and X twenty one dual clocking. Link protocols use hex values two zero zero zero through two zero zero C in listed order for HDLC, PPP, Cisco HDLC, Frame Relay, Frame Relay add and delete PVC, X twenty five, HDLC Ethernet emulation, Frame Relay add and delete Ethernet bridged PVC, Frame Relay PVC status read, Frame Relay Ethernet PVC, and raw socket.

Operational state enumerates seven values in order unknown, not present, down, lower layer down, testing, dormant, and up. Link mode enumerates three values in order default, dormant limited to prevent upward move beyond dormant, and testing limited to prevent upward move beyond testing.

Device memory mapping holds memory start then memory end as unsigned long, base address as unsigned short, then one byte each for interrupt, direct memory access channel, and port, with three spare bytes implied for alignment.

Device and protocol settings carry a type selector and a caller allocated data size as unsigned integers, followed by a union of user space pointers to raw HDLC, Cisco, Frame Relay, Frame Relay PVC, Frame Relay PVC info, X twenty five, synchronous serial, and T or E one specific settings structures, only one of which is meaningful per request.

Interface request carries a first union holding the interface name array, and a second union offering alternative payloads sharing storage such as socket addresses for local, peer, broadcast, netmask and hardware address, short flags, integer value reused for metric, transmit unit, index, bandwidth and queue length, device map, slave name, new name, user data pointer, and embedded device settings. Short alias names expose each nested member directly, for example name, hardware address, address variants, flags, metric, transmit unit, map, slave, data, index, bandwidth, queue length, new name, and settings.

Interface configuration list carries an integer buffer length plus a union that is either a user character buffer pointer or a user array pointer of interface requests. Two aliases expose the union arms as buffer address and request array.
Address netlink header orders one byte each for family, prefix length, flags, and scope, followed by a thirty two bit link index.

Address attributes enumerate from zero as unspecified, address, local, label, broadcast, anycast, cache info, multicast, flags, route priority as unsigned thirty two, target network namespace identifier, protocol as unsigned eight, and multicast user count as unsigned thirty two, with a sentinel marking the end and a maximum defined as one less than that sentinel.

Address flags use hex one for secondary which also names temporary, two for no duplicate address detection, four for optimistic, eight for duplicate detection failed, ten hex for home address, twenty hex for deprecated, forty hex for tentative, eighty hex for permanent, one hundred hex for manage temporary address, two hundred hex for no prefix route, four hundred hex for multicast auto join, and eight hundred hex for stable privacy. Address origin uses zero for unspecified, one for kernel loopback, two for kernel router advertisement, and three for kernel link local.
Address cache info holds four unsigned thirty two bit values in order preferred lifetime, valid lifetime, creation stamp, and update stamp, where stamps count hundredths of seconds.
Attribute access derives the first routing attribute by advancing past the aligned size of the address header, and payload length is the netlink payload remaining after that header.

Bonding user API reports application binary interface version two. Legacy control numbers build on the private device ioctl base with offsets zero for enslave, one for release, two for set hardware address, eleven for slave info query, twelve for info query, and thirteen for change active, while link status check reuses the media independent interface query. Bonding modes number zero through six as round robin, active backup, exclusive or, broadcast, eight zero two point three ad, transmit load balancing, and adaptive load balancing.

Bonding slave link reports zero up and running, one just failed, two long down, and three returning. Slave role is zero active and one backup. Defaults are one maximum bond, sixteen transmit queues per device, and one group management resend. Transmit hash policies number zero through five as layer two, layer three plus four, layer two plus three, encapsulated two plus three, encapsulated three plus four, and virtual LAN plus source media address. Aggregation control state bits use hex one, two, four, eight, ten, twenty, forty, and eighty for activity, timeout, aggregation, synchronization, collecting, distributing, defaulted, and expired.

Bonding info carries mode, slave count, and monitor interval as signed thirty two. Slave info carries numeric identifier, interface name sized text, one byte link code, one byte role, and unsigned thirty two link failure count. Aggregator info carries sixteen bit aggregator identifier, port count, actor key, and partner key, plus a partner system address sized as an Ethernet address. Extended statistics enumerate an unspecified value then aggregation with a maximum one less than sentinel, and aggregation counters enumerate receive and transmit counts for control and marker protocol events plus padding with a maximum one less than sentinel.

Ethernet user API fixes address at six octets, type field at two, header at fourteen, minimum frame without check at sixty, maximum payload at fifteen hundred, maximum frame without check at fifteen fourteen, check sequence at four, minimum Internet Protocol version four transmit unit at sixty eight, and maximum transmit unit at sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five.

Ethernet type registry first group assigns hex 0060 loop, 0200 PUP, 0201 PUP address translation, 22F0 time sensitive networking, 22EB encapsulated span two, 0800 Internet Protocol, 0805 X twenty five, 0806 address resolution, 08FF BPQ, 0A00 and 0A01 IEEE PUP variants, 4305 BATMAN, 6000 through 6007 DEC family in order assigned, dump load, remote console, routing, local area transport, diagnostics, customer use, communications architecture, 6558 transparent bridging, and 8035 reverse address resolution.

Ethernet type registry second group assigns hex 809B Appletalk, 80F3 Appletalk address resolution, 8100 virtual LAN, 88BE encapsulated span, 8137 IPX, 86DD Internet Protocol version six, 8808 pause, 8809 slow protocols, 883E cache coordination, 8847 and 8848 multiprotocol label switching unicast and multicast, 884C multiprotocol over ATM, 8863 and 8864 point to point over Ethernet discovery and session, 886C link control, 8870 eight zero two point one AC, 8884 ATM over Ethernet, 888E port access, and 8892 PROFINET.

Ethernet type registry third group assigns hex 8899 Realtek, 88A2 ATA over Ethernet, 88A4 EtherCAT, 88A8 service VLAN, 88B5 local experimental one, 88C3 MaxLinear switch, 88C7 preauthentication, 88CA TIPC, 88CC discovery, 88E3 redundancy, 88E5 MAC security, 88E7 backbone tag, 88F5 registration, 88F7 timing, 88F8 sideband, 88FB parallel redundancy, 8902 fault management, 8906 Fibre Channel, and 8915 Infiniband.

Ethernet type registry final group assigns hex 890D tunneled direct link, 8914 Fibre Channel init, 8917 media independent handover, 892F high availability seamless redundancy, 894F service header, 9000 loopback, 9100 through 9300 deprecated stacked VLAN variants, 9988 Motorcomm switch, DADA and DADB distributed switch tags, E001 A5 switch tag, ED3E forwarding element, FBFB IBM IUCV, and FD3A NXP switch. Value hex 0600 is the threshold where larger type values mean Ethernet Two framing and smaller values mean eight zero two point three length framing.
Each user header defines a single inclusion guard macro that marks the header as seen to prevent repeated inclusion.
Device flag documentation distinguishes file system managed flags from volatile kernel managed flags, and availability is gated by user API feature macros for compatibility with system libraries.

Several requests reuse storage through unions so only one arm is valid at a time. In particular the integer payload of interface requests aliases metric, transmit unit, index, bandwidth, and queue length, and configuration and settings unions alias buffer against request array and protocol specific pointers, so writing one view overwrites the others and reading the wrong arm yields unrelated bits.
